 AirAsia names Bahrain board, sets March deadline for flights
 AirAsia names Bahrain board, sets March deadline for flights
 01-Nov-2026, 22:04 01 Nov 2026, 22:04 FMT Reporters Share The airline's advisor, Tony Fernandes, said Bahrain is strategically important to the group as the gateway connecting Asean with the Middle East, Europe and beyond.
 AirAsia announced in February this year that Bahrain would be its Middle Eastern hub. (EPA Images pic) 
 PETALING JAYA : AirAsia Group has named a board of directors for its Bahrain operations, and hopes to begin flights to the Gulf nation by March as part of its regional expansion, the company said today. 
 In a statement today, AirAsia Group, formerly known as AirAsia X Bhd, said the board will be chaired by Dr Serra Kirdar, with Fam Lee Ee as vice-chairman, Bernama reported. The non-executive directors are Faisal Khalid Kanoo, Nawaf Al Zayani, Akram Safa, Lord Ahmad of Wimbledon and Jamaludin Ibrahim.
 The airline’s owner, Capital A Bhd, reached an agreement with the Bahrain government in November 2025 and announced in February this year that Bahrain would be its Middle Eastern hub.
 AirAsia Group advisor and Capital A chief executive officer Tony Fernandes said Bahrain is strategically important to the group as the gateway connecting Asean with the Middle East, Europe and beyond.
